method: AI-assisted, full-body primary-source review in disjoint page worklists, followed by editorial reconciliation of every reported outcome, exact body and capture hashes, heading and code-fence accounting, consequential primary-source spot checks, and bounded independently reproduced example checks. This record is a projection of completed reviews, not an automated factual certification.
limitations: Research cutoff is September 14, 2026 in the editorial locale for the OS 27 general-availability pages reviewed in this pass; all other pages retain their September 8, 2026 cutoff and state it in their own record. Actual retrieval and consolidation timestamps may fall later in UTC; they do not redate source publication or a page's research cutoff.

Some later mutable-source confirmations lack identical pre-cutoff captures and cannot establish exact cutoff bytes. These entries are explicitly marked; the editorial release baseline is not silently advanced.

Reviews are AI-assisted, not human approval or a guarantee against factual error. Mutable primary sources may later differ. Raw source hashes bind the inspected captures; raw third-party source bodies and private execution artifacts are not redistributed. Explicitly rejected destinations and documentation shells are negative or routing evidence, not factual support for API claims.

Exact Apple documentation contradictions are retained where meaningful; framework landing metadata does not override concrete symbol availability, runtime hardware, entitlement, region or service restrictions.

Every page states its actual code-example review scope. Source comparison, parsing, type-checking, mocked checks and runtime execution are different evidence; none implies every linked upstream project or service was exercised.
No local Xcode 27/Swift 6.4 or OS 27 runtime, earliest OS 26.0 runtime, physical-device/live-service suite, comprehensive visual-accessibility review, or hosted workflow execution was completed.
The source review does not establish redistribution rights for documentation, design images or sample photographs. Existing asset-rights uncertainties remain explicit in metadata/assets.json.

On September 23, 2026, hard-wrapped prose was joined onto single lines in 15 reviewed pages and in the generated-index paragraph template in scripts/docs.py, and those pages' content_sha256 values and 13 evidence hashes for scripts/docs.py and LICENSE were re-stamped without repeating the full-body review. The change is whitespace-only: for every re-stamped page the text with whitespace collapsed and the HTML rendered by markdown-it and by pandoc are identical before and after, and scripts/docs.py changed only by joining the seven string literals of that one paragraph with spaces. The previously reviewed bytes are at commit b5a7b58.

On September 26, 2026, README.md's shared-layout edit (commit 3af78bb) received a targeted review of what it changed, recorded in that page's changes and qualifications, and the review restored the dropped limit on its MIT statement. The same day, the Catalog scope paragraph template in scripts/docs.py baseline_section was joined onto one line to match that edit, and the scripts/docs.py evidence hashes of the 11 other records citing it were re-stamped without repeating their reviews; no statement those records support with scripts/docs.py depends on the line breaks of that paragraph. The change is whitespace-only: the old and new baseline_section outputs differ only by two newlines becoming spaces inside that paragraph, and generated_indexes output is byte-identical. The previously reviewed bytes are at commit 08b6a70.

UsageInformation required schemaVersion number allowed1, merchantName, matching merchantTokenIdentifier and modificationDate; expiration optional<=one year ahead.

changes: Corrected Catalyst and async-interface availability, device capability scope and misleading all-hardware wording.
Removed orphaned/fixed-label permission screenshot description; use actual authorization state instead.
Added actual27 placemark deprecation separately from26 geocoder deprecation.
Corrected CLCondition interface type and removed unsupported alternate-region-key deprecation.
Clarified background platform restrictions, service-session role and qualified location-push error namespace.
numerical_and_availability_checks: CLLocationManager platform annotations verify original framework scope and Catalyst13.1, not inherited13.0.
liveUpdates and Objective-C CLLocationUpdater are mobile/Catalyst/tv17, macOS14, visionOS1, watchOS10; neither is inherently new27.
CLGeocoder formally deprecated26; CLPlacemark separately deprecated27 across listed platforms, recommending GeoToolbox/MapKit. Neither declaration marks removal.
Swift CLCondition is a Decodable/Encodable/Sendable protocol although its abstract says base class; Objective-C CLCondition is an actual NSObject class.
kCLErrorUserInfoAlternateRegionKey has no formal deprecation annotation or summary; inherited Deprecated tag removed. CLRegion remains documented without a class deprecation.
NSLocationDefaultAccuracyReduced is supported/nondeprecated; default false and person can change precision. No promise that every service works under reduced accuracy.
NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription metadata marks mobile deprecation10 but discussion retains it for targets before11 alongside newer key; no invented one-date replacement/removal rule.
Always access unavailable on tvOS/visionOS; visionOS has no background updates; watchOS Always does not launch apps; macOS access levels are functionally equivalent.
Location push extension starts mobile15, requires entitlement/Always and is rate constrained; no unlimited polling or consent bypass.

CLServiceSession expresses authorization goals and exposes diagnostics; the session does not prove permission granted. Hardware and RunLoop/delegate requirements read in complete manager/configuration bodies.
qualifications: Primary async sample metadata says Xcode15.3 while its setup body requires Xcode16; local page has no compiler baseline or copied sample.

Background guide spells explicit-session key NSLocationRequireExplicitServiceSession; suspension guide uses CLRequireExplicitServiceSession. Neither spelling nor inconsistent sample initializer is copied into local instructions.
Original permission-image wording was an old primary alt description, not a reliable current prompt; it has been removed.
No local code fences or device-location, permission, geofence, beacon, push or network-geocoding operations executed.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Loader is Sendable. ArrayLoader, JSONLoader, StreamLoader and SampleGenerator actor roles checked from definitions. JSONLoader logs/skips decoding failures but throws file-open errors; require input-count checks.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Read Metric, Evaluator, MetricsAggregator, EvaluationResult, ResultColumn and related aggregate/typed-column declarations. ignore excludes a result; aggregator supports mean/max/grouping. detailed is DataFrame; groupedSummary is formatted output. aggregateValue returns -1 if absent, so require metric-presence checks.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Read ModelJudgeEvaluator, ScoreDimension, ModelJudgePrompt and complete model-as-judge workflow. Pointwise/pairwise and multiple dimensions are real; recommendations distinguish subjective judging from ground truth.

Added separate verified availability for the dimming preference query, flashing-light processor and Music Haptics manager; retained the existing overview, three feature topics and Source footer.
Corrected the two earlier superseded topic destinations during the preceding full-body audit.
Corrected 2 superseded/misdirected external-link targets using captured primary destinations.
numerical_and_availability_checks: Framework landing metadata reports iOS/iPadOS/tvOS 17 and Catalyst 13.0, but it is not the legacy caption API minimum; the discrepancy remains explicitly documented.

Concrete GetDisplayType, SetDisplayType, CopySelectedLanguages and CopyForegroundColor references show iOS/iPadOS 7.0, Catalyst 13.1, macOS 10.9 and visionOS 1.0. Their current web metadata still reports tvOS 17.

Installed AppleTVOS26.5/iPhoneOS26.5 MACaptionAppearance.h declares the four legacy APIs with CF_AVAILABLE(10_9, 7_0). Clang reports an implicit unversioned tvOS availability, and strict syntax-only checks pass at tvOS 9.0 and iOS 7.0 deployment targets; no tvOS 9 runtime execution is claimed.
MADimFlashingLightsEnabled: iOS/iPadOS/Catalyst/tvOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, visionOS 1.0.
MAFlashingLightsProcessor: iOS/iPadOS/Catalyst/tvOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, visionOS 1.0; it is separate from the earlier preference query.

MAMusicHapticsManager: iOS/iPadOS/Catalyst/tvOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, visionOS 2.0. isActive and checkHapticTrackAvailabilityForMedia(matchingCode:completionHandler:) distinguish settings and song support from mere symbol availability.
qualifications: Current concrete web caption metadata still lists tvOS 17. The SDK header has CF_AVAILABLE(10_9, 7_0), not a literal tvOS 9 annotation; its unversioned inherited tvOS availability and successful 9.0-target declaration check support the legacy baseline. No old-device runtime test was performed.

Caption baseline availability does not lower newer Flashing Lights or Music Haptics requirements; platform metadata does not establish usable haptic hardware, enabled settings or a matching haptic track.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Complete endpoint and event/metadata/art/card schemas read; field requirements, optional card data and exact relationship roles checked.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Complete unlink endpoint/request reviewed:204, no additional info, merchant-specific invalidation prevents future authorizations.

sections_reviewed.assessment: Read required errorMessage/statusCode/subStatusCode fields and endpoint-specific use, including202 key response.

changes: Corrected blanket merchant-token issuance, linked all six native/web payment-request types including deferred requests.
Documented actual GET notification suffix, acknowledgment/retry and seven-day retrieval semantics.
Added precise required headers and204/no-body invalidation versus refund distinction.
Added metadata update and owner-key event/recovery handling; fixed topic labels and linked concrete object schemas.
numerical_and_availability_checks: Full root/tap-and-pull behavior: event details available seven days; notifications identify events rather than carrying payment/charge payloads.

Actual inbound method GET; Apple appends /notification/merchantToken/{eventId} to the supplied baseURL. TLS>=1.2;200 even unknown event/token,500 inability to process; up to3 immediate retries after non200.
Merchant-to-Apple mTLS separate from device-to-merchant TLS/authenticationToken and App Store JWTs. Required Content-Type/x-request-id verified on Apple-hosted endpoints.
Invalidate Merchant Token returns204/no body; invalid merchant/token400;500 server error. Invalidates future authorizations, not refunding prior charges.
Public-key202 accepted-not-ready is not a200 key response;409 signals notification metadata conflict; UPDATED_MERCHANT_TOKEN_PUBLIC_KEY is actual event enum.

Automatic-reload network fallback produces device token, not universal merchant-token issuance. Native recurring/reload16/mobile+13/mac; deferred16.4/mobile+13.3/mac; no blanket framework/OS27 minimum applied.
Card metadata optional fields describe card expiration/suffix; no full PAN claim; reason/eventType/tokenID required in concrete event schema.
qualifications: Root/older endpoints carry a misleading App Store Connect API platform tag alongside Merchant Token Management API1.0.12. Local uses actual merchant service/authentication rather than deriving ASC credentials or OS deployment requirements.
Root and receiving guide overgeneralize token issuance; concrete automatic-reload and deferred requests qualify it by network support. Local follows the concrete contract.
Notifications may be duplicated; idempotent processing/queue persistence are integration recommendations, not an exactly-once delivery guarantee.
No merchant/server/account operations, invalidation, authentication or private-key handling executed.

Tap to Share integration guide mentions PaymentCardReader.Token without documenting the complete wrapping step. Concrete open argument and Token.init(using:) resolve this precisely, rather than inventing an implicit conversion.

Tap-to-Pay entitlement setup prose confusingly refers to adding entitlements to Info.plist; local follows its concrete signed.entitlements/managed-capability steps, not a fabricated plist permission mechanism.

Several source guide snippets are illustrative or malformed: stored property in extension, nonasync functions containingawait, try await let syntax, unresolved sample helpers and placeholder payment processing. None copied as runnable code.
Verifier token article describes decoded header/payload separately; local does not imply those two JSON objects alone are a complete signed JWT or a48-hour exp value.

The guessed payment.acceptance DocC entitlement symbol URL returned404. It is excluded from source evidence; the full official setup guide explicitly supplies the key/Boolean/approval/distribution contract.404 does not establish API removal.
Entire text/metadata/field/declaration bodies of42 linked primary topics plus15 focused contracts and root reviewed. No sample ZIP/runtime entitlement/device/payment validation performed or claimed.

sections_reviewed.heading: Entitlement refresh and restoration
sections_reviewed.assessment: Full currentEntitlements/updates/finish/sync/willAutoRenew/expirationDate bodies reread. Startup listener and same-device purchase result are separate paths; fulfill before finish; current entitled state differs from future renewal, refunded/revoked history and consumables. Modern StoreKit auto-syncs/reinstalls; sync() is only explicit user action with authentication prompt, then re-evaluate current verified entitlements. Legacy restoring guide not generalized to modern APIs.

Active local or synced.storekit uses locally generated Xcode-signed data; selectingNone enables real catalog/sandbox configuration. No universal subscription speed, regional policy orDEBUG-as-environment inference. Precise account-mode follow-up: development-signed iOS/iPadOS uses Settings>Developer sandbox sign-in after a purchase attempt without needing non-Sandbox sign-out. TestFlight IAP already uses sandbox; iOS sandbox-control setup requires Media&Purchases sign-out and Developer sandbox sign-in. Content-access warning/dedicated-device suggestion retained. Not an always/never sign-out rule or an iCloud sign-out instruction.

General SemanticTags metadata iOS/iPadOS12/watch5 predates27; individual semantic layouts/fields later. Dedicated boarding guide iOS/watch26 with semanticBoardingPass/PKTransitTypeAir and required tags; legacy fields needed for fallback.
Poster-event guide warns incompatible with QR/barcode-entry tickets; new layout not a universal alternative to every existing ticket style.
Manifest uses SHA1 per relative source file and detached PKCS7 signature; no invented SHA256 manifest migration. formatVersion number1 and six general required Pass fields read.
Pass-type and serial-number pair uniquely identify/replace pass. Update guide retains pass type, serial and authentication token; registrations are many-to-many, not global pass deletion.

Production HTTPS and production-only pass-update APNs; empty JSON notification, separate list/fetch operation. ApplePass authorization for register/unregister/get; listing authenticated with device-library shared secret.
Registration201 new/200 already registered/401 unauthenticated; list200 JSON or204 no matches; passGET200 application/vnd.apple.pkpass/401; unregister200/401.
SerialNumbers.lastUpdated is developer-defined string; actual request query passesUpdatedSince uses it. Not a required Unix timestamp or literal previousLastUpdated query key.

UpcomingPassInformationEntry introduced26, required identifier/name/type with type allowed event; isActive defaultfalse; omitted dateInformation yieldsTBD. EntryType helper image objects are not the entry list/type enum.
Personalization POST200 application/octet-stream signed token; PersonalizationDictionary requires personalizationToken and requiredPersonalizationInfo. Not a replacement pass response.
Distribution guide states up to10passes or150MB bundle; local introduces no new interpretation. Broad generic field counts/modern-field dates contain source conflicts and were not generalized.

UpcomingEntry and personalization abstracts are misleading relative to concrete properties/response; local follows those full schemas.

Endpoint metadata marks ApplePass Authorization optional, but update guide requires shared-secret authentication and endpoints document401. Local follows authenticated production workflow, not unsafe anonymous personalized retrieval.

sections_reviewed.heading: Framework Usage
sections_reviewed.assessment: Read every linked framework-usage report in full including all distinct field/glossary rows. Corrected sampled counts, configured images, Photos prompt scope, picker scope, CoreML loading, Metal concurrency, Safari enabled-device counts, Wallet requested retention—not identity values, PiP exclusion, browser-choice version/cohort distinctions and Wi-Fi updates.

sections_reviewed.heading: Performance
sections_reviewed.assessment: Read all17 performance reports completely. Corrected disk byte volume, launch-image-vs-app failure, expanded crashes and selected-app streaming coverage; checked differing units and200-download/session privacy thresholds without inventing universal limits.

code_examples.verification: No local code fences or live authenticated operations. Full inline workflow/field/endpoint contracts source-checked; all linked report descriptions compared with complete primary bodies.

changes: Repaired120 topic destinations from actual primary relationships, including non-mechanical aliases for privacy, completeness, downloads, pre-orders, purchases and installs.
Corrected request/report/instance/segment hierarchy, credential role distinctions and inactive-request recovery.
Added first-report delay, five-minute download URLs, truthful retention/snapshot limits and scoped completeness/privacy parsing guidance.
Corrected23 report summaries for actual measured quantities, cohorts, availability and failure objects while retaining all useful verified summaries.
numerical_and_availability_checks: Analytics service/request endpoints have their own versions; no universal OS17.4/27 baseline inferred from report pipeline history. Platform/territory coverage differs by report.
Only ADMIN creates/deletes requests; ADMIN/SALES_AND_REPORTS/FINANCE read. SALES_AND_REPORTS cannot download finance reports.
First reports1–2days; instances35days; one snapshot request per month; no fixed30-day reinterpretation or unlimited historical recovery.
Concrete segment endpoint states URL lifetime5minutes, distinct from instance retention; list endpoints have maximum200 resources per page, not total report rows.

Daily instances may contain multiple dates; weekly Monday–Sunday and Date starts week; monthly Date starts month. Newer processing versions replace older partitions only for report types covered by central completeness rules.
Video PiP excludes sessions<=8seconds. Older browser-choice report EU iOS before18.2; newer EU iOS/iPadOS18.2+. Default-browser usage observes devices weekly despite daily file availability.
Streaming download/playback reports require at least200 downloads/unique playback sessions per datapoint for selected apps; do not apply generic5-device/event thresholds universally.
Symbols are sampled appearances; detection images are configured counts; storage fields are bytes; Photos prompt responses are not grant-type rows; Wallet fields are requested retention settings.

ARKit throttling full body/field measures time until throttling, not throttled duration. Translation Request Usage full primary explicitly says speech-to-text; retained as that report's own terminology.
Per-report duration units/histogram bucket codes/SDK glossary checked; no SDK enum mapping, exact invocation counters, financial settlement promise or all-row unique-user sums invented.
qualifications: All120 linked topic pages read:118 reports plus two guides. Exact duplicate paragraphs/table rows reused by hash;1693 unique blocks reviewed, complete original source-to-block relationships retained.
No guarantee every report is returned for every app; report-specific coverage/cohorts and availability apply.
Primary examples occasionally use generic historical dates or repeated SDK/platform boilerplate; no runtime availability inferred from those.
Full primary field tables contain internal/SPI or categorical labels; they are report values, not an advertised public API surface.
This is a documentation/content audit, not live report generation, downloading customer analytics, or external service execution.

Reviewed guidance and examples, including: - **Customize a slider's appearance if it adds value** - You can adjust a slider's appearance — including track color, thumb image and tint color, and left and right icons — to blend with your app's design and communicate intent. A slider that adjusts image size, for example, could show a small image icon on the left and a large image icon on the right. - **

sections_reviewed.heading: Platform Considerations
sections_reviewed.assessment: Upstream: Platform considerations. Reviewed guidance and examples, including: **iOS, iPadOS** - Don't use a slider to adjust audio volume. If you need to provide volume control in your app, use a volume view, which is customizable and includes a volume-level slider and a control for changing the active audio output device. For guidance, see [Playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio). *

sections_reviewed.heading: Updating Widget Content
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed every reload/freshness/date/relevance/placeholder/animation/Live Activity paragraph. Extension is not continuously active; timelines, reload requests and opportunistically budgeted WidgetKit push updates are distinct. Push supplements timelines. Relevance is not guaranteed placement. ActivityKit lifecycle is not simply the widget timeline mechanism or an unrestricted stream.

changes: Corrected larger-text percentage meaning using current App Store criteria.
Replaced overbroad all-bold 3:1 claim with scoped WCAG criteria and explicit source discrepancy; separated native-app evaluation.
Distinguished spoken descriptions, Music Haptics and audible Audio graphs.
Fixed Nutrition Labels destination and replaced index-redirecting video with verified WWDC26 session.
Labeled Apple article history and fixed the Assistive Access example typo.
numerical_and_availability_checks: Font default/minimum pt rows verified: iOS/iPadOS 17/11; macOS 13/10; tvOS 29/23; visionOS 17/12; watchOS 16/12.

Control default/minimum pt dimensions verified: iOS/iPadOS 44x44/28x28; macOS 28x28/20x20; tvOS 66x66/56x56; visionOS 60x60/28x28; watchOS 44x44/28x28. Approximate 12-pt bezel / 24-pt no-bezel padding matches primary general guidance.
Larger Text criteria specify final size at least 200% of default or system maximum; watchOS largest Dynamic Type exceeds 140% of default. Fixed ambiguity between final size and percentage added.

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3: normal text 4.5:1; large-scale 3:1, with 18 CSS pt regular or 14 CSS pt bold thresholds and defined incidental/inactive/logo exceptions. Native layout points are not automatically CSS pt.
Primary HIG All/Bold -> 3:1 row conflicts with W3C large-text definition. Both raw sources saved and the difference explicitly explained rather than copying a false WCAG rule.
Apple native Sufficient Contrast criteria allow evaluated Increase Contrast/custom alternatives and are distinguished from claiming generic WCAG conformance.
Music Haptics requires known supported tracks and active feature state; Audio graphs encode chart axes as sound, not a general haptic output API.
Full Keyboard Access/Voice Control/Switch Control and autoplay/flash/Assistive Access linked feature descriptions checked; specific UIKit autoplay API availability was not generalized to watchOS.
Five historical dates (June 9 2025, March 7 2025, June 10 2024, December 5 2023, June 21 2023) and descriptions match primary Change log.
qualifications: The current HIG contrast table is simplified and differs from W3C large-text requirements; this is explicitly documented with both primary captures.
HIG platform text-size recommendations do not imply an identical Dynamic Type setting or Nutrition Label on macOS.

sections_reviewed.heading: Augmented Reality
sections_reviewed.assessment: Read complete definition and platform header against primary abstract. Header identifies HIG experience scope, not a universal framework availability matrix.

sections_reviewed.heading: Overview
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed live-camera/device-motion/multiuser explanation, capability checking, optional-AR eligibility, handheld scope note and contrast/motion/accessibility paragraphs. Corrected handheld camera architecture versus provider-based visionOS; retained runtime capability checking without importing the device-support article’s outdated TrueDepth-only face-tracking statement.

sections_reviewed.heading: Topics
sections_reviewed.assessment: Structural wrapper; all substantive children and nested bold guidance independently assessed.

upstream_positions.scope: Nonfactual navigation wrapper; actual primary content hierarchy.

sections_reviewed.heading: Best Practices
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed all display-space, realistic-assets/scale/light/shadow/grain, reflection approximations, audio/haptics, minimal text, indirect controls, Measure example, environmental requirements, fatigue, progressive motion and safety recommendations against HIG. Corrected screen-space versus world coordinates using ARAnchor and overlaySKScene terminology; qualified 60 updates/second as HIG design target, not a device/rendering guarantee. VideoFormat framesPerSecond describes capture/AR-frame delivery, not guaranteed renderer cadence.

sections_reviewed.heading: Providing Coaching
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed initial setup/relocalization, hiding controls, custom goals and horizontal/vertical plane guidance. activatesAutomatically is true by default for a configured ARCoachingOverlayView and follows goals/session state; removed implication every AR session automatically supplies coaching UI.

sections_reviewed.heading: Helping People Place Objects
sections_reviewed.assessment: Read all surface indicators, alignment, immediate placement/refinement, offscreen audio/visual cues, approximate boundaries and classification examples. ARTrackedRaycast produces ongoing refined results; removed final surface-detection completion guarantee. isClassificationSupported makes table/floor classification conditional; unsupported/unclassified results need fallback.

sections_reviewed.heading: Designing Object Interactions
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed all direct/indirect manipulation contexts, one-finger drag/two-finger rotation examples, 2D touch versus 3D movement, near-target tolerance, furniture-versus-fantasy scaling, scale-versus-distance tip, gesture conflicts, surface-constrained motion and motion/proximity input. These are HIG design recommendations, not automatic ARKit gestures or an exhaustive interaction API list.

sections_reviewed.heading: Offering a Multiuser Experience
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed the three inherited paragraphs against primary collaboration and person-occlusion discussions: consistent shared placement requires implementation/state exchange, occlusion is hardware-capability dependent, and late joining must account for participant tracking. No built-in transport, automatic all-client synchronization or universal people segmentation claimed.

sections_reviewed.heading: Reacting to Real-World Objects
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed reference data/recognition examples, image detection/tracking, loss grace period, candidate-set batching and tracking-resource guidance. Corrected no-image-position-tracking claim: world tracking default maximumNumberOfTrackedImages=0 still permits infrequent detected-anchor updates; nonzero continuously tracks up to four simultaneously. ARImageTrackingConfiguration is distinct and not assigned that universal maximum. Around 100 reference images is a performance recommendation; updated sets require rerunning configuration.

sections_reviewed.heading: Communicating with People
sections_reviewed.assessment: Read all four approachable-language table rows, contextual 3D hints, fallback textual instructions, readable labels and more-information cues. Rephrased 3D text sizing to maintain readable apparent size rather than conflating world distance and fixed geometric size. No tracking diagnostic is presented as a guaranteed cure.

sections_reviewed.heading: Handling Interruptions
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed tracking loss, previous-placement validity, recovery coaching, hiding stale content, keeping furniture customization in AR, cancel/reset, and face-loss feedback. Lifecycle source explains visual-inertial tracking and potentially indefinite relocalization; changed absolute failure/success language to conditional recovery. Half-second face feedback is HIG timing advice and scoped to supported face-tracking experiences.

sections_reviewed.heading: Suggesting Problem Resolutions
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed reset option and all three cause/suggestion table rows: insufficient features/light, excessive motion, and long surface detection. Suggestions remain possibilities, not guaranteed fixes or invented diagnostics.

sections_reviewed.heading: Icons and Badges
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed every glyph/badge use, modification restriction, collapsed/expanded treatment, redundant all-AR badging, consistent corner placement, and both 10%-of-height clear-space statements against actual primary HIG prose. Confirmed meaningful Apple Design Resources destination. No asset download, alteration, or new license/provenance claim.

sections_reviewed.heading: Platform Considerations
sections_reviewed.assessment: Reviewed all platform prose. Removed universal unsupported-on-macOS claim because ARKitSession and WorldTrackingProvider declarations include macOS 26; SDK presence does not imply standalone Mac hardware/data support. visionOS provider support, distinct hand/world-sensing authorization, denial/revocation and alternative input are supported by the specific privacy guide. Did not imply automatic access to raw passthrough pixels.

sections_reviewed.heading: Related Components
sections_reviewed.assessment: Verified the meaningful primary HIG playing-haptics and gestures relationships. No video/title agreement substituted for the preceding body review.

sections_reviewed.heading: Developer Documentation
sections_reviewed.assessment: Verified ARKit root and actual continuous-image-tracking, image-only configuration, and video-format declaration bodies. SceneKit overlay evidence was used for terminology, not added as a new-framework recommendation.

sections_reviewed.heading: Historical API Context
sections_reviewed.assessment: The actual HIG has no change-log section supporting the inherited version-based article-history assertions. Replaced these with explicitly sourced framework-availability context, preserving useful history without inventing HIG update dates.

sections_reviewed.heading: visionOS 1.0
sections_reviewed.assessment: ARKitSession and WorldTrackingProvider declarations introduce the provider-based interface at visionOS 1.0; later providers have individual availability. No assertion that all sensing capabilities shipped in 1.0.

sections_reviewed.heading: iOS 11.0
sections_reviewed.assessment: ARKit and ARWorldTrackingConfiguration declarations introduce the base mobile framework at iOS 11.0. Removed unsupported claim that the HIG itself established basic guidelines on that release date.

code_examples.verification: Complete body, all bold subsections, tables, examples, resources and historical assertions read. Inline APIs source-verified; no code fences or runtime/device tests.

changes: Corrected coordinates, rendering-rate guarantees, coaching/placement lifecycle and semantic-classification assumptions.
Corrected image detection versus continuous tracking and scoped numerical recommendations.
Qualified relocalization/face-feedback behavior and SDK-versus-HIG platform scope; replaced invented article history with genuine API history.
Improved source links and removed stray Apple glyph without changing artwork.
numerical_and_availability_checks: 60 scene updates/second: HIG handheld target, not a guarantee or identity with capture framesPerSecond.

World tracking: maximumNumberOfTrackedImages defaults 0; nonzero tracks up to four images simultaneously. Zero still permits infrequent detection-anchor position updates. Distinct image-only configurations are not assigned that limit.
detectionImages: around 100 or fewer recommended for accuracy/performance; not a hard capacity limit; rerun the configuration after changing the set.
Tracking-loss UX: up to one second image fade grace and roughly half a second face feedback are HIG recommendations, not API timers.
Plane classification: actual capability query and unsupported results checked; no universal model-based promise.
Glyph and badge clear space independently verified as 10% of their respective heights.
ARKit/world-tracking base iOS 11; provider-session/world tracking visionOS 1 and macOS 26 per individual declarations; no inference that all APIs/devices share support.
qualifications: The device-support source contains an outdated TrueDepth-only face-tracking description; no such model restriction was imported. Specific capability checks govern the local guidance.
Current primary HIG experience scope is narrower than some current ARKit symbol declarations; page explicitly separates them.
No AR hardware, camera stream, tracking recovery, gestures or image assets were exercised; verification is documentary, not runtime.
